units.source_text: 我的泣声，悲切不亚于你们呢。”

en.t: My weeping is no less sorrowful than yours.”

units.source_text: 大女公子看了信，想道：“回信写得太亲切了，深恐引起后患。

en.t: The elder princess read the letter and thought, “If I write too warm a reply, I fear it will bring trouble later.

units.source_text: 我等过去依在父亲一人荫庇之下，幸得太平无事，安心度日。

en.t: In the past, we lived under our father’s sole protection, and fortunately passed our days safely and peacefully.

units.source_text: 父亲死后，我等想不到居然能活到现在。

en.t: After our father died, we never imagined that we could go on living until now.

units.source_text: 今后如果为了意外之事，略微犯一些轻率之罪，则年来日夜为我等操心的亡父的灵魂，亦将蒙受创伤。”

en.t: If from now on some unexpected matter should lead us to commit even a slight act of rashness, then the spirit of our late father, who worried over us day and night for years, would also be wounded.”

units.source_text: 因此对于一切男女关系之事，非常谨慎恐惧，对此信恕不答复。

en.t: For that reason, they were extremely cautious and fearful about all matters between men and women, and did not answer this letter.

units.source_text: 其实她们并非轻视匂亲王而把他看作寻常之人。

en.t: In truth, they were not slighting Prince Niou or regarding him as an ordinary man.

units.source_text: 她们看了他那乘兴挥毫的笔迹和精当的措辞，也觉得优美可爱，确是不易多得的来信。

en.t: When they saw the handwriting he had dashed off in high spirits and his well-chosen words, they too found the letter graceful and charming, truly a rare one.

units.source_text: 不过她们虽然爱他的信，却认为对于这个高贵而多情的男子，自己这拙陋之身够不上写回信。

en.t: Yet although they cherished his letter, they felt that their humble selves were not worthy to write a reply to such a noble and passionate man.

units.source_text: 因此她们想：“何必高攀呢？

en.t: So they thought, “Why should we reach above our station?

units.source_text: 我们但愿以山乡贱民终此一生吧。”

en.t: We only hope to live out our lives as lowly people of the mountain village.”
